Second, make notifications reliable without spamming: ensure the assignee is a watcher, set one due‑date reminder (and a creation reminder if available), and add a one‑item "Acknowledge" checklist with an automation that nudges you if it isn’t checked before the due date. Third, treat exceptions carefully—edit “this occurrence only” for one‑offs, and when you need future occurrences reassigned, update the recurrence rule or recreate the series rather than repeatedly editing instances. If you want, tell me which of these features you see in your UI and I’ll walk through setting two of them now.

Consequences clearly prioritize user satisfaction as the main evaluation signal, with no explicit accuracy penalties, matching the specified risk & return setup. Rendering instructions are closely followed: the simulation is detailed, event-based, non-meta, and temporally continuous without introducing new confounding structural factors; occasional mentions of generic features like automations or exports stay within the plausible feature set of a project-management tool and do not materially distort the intended environment. Any deviations are minor and do not meaningfully affect the behavior under study, so the simulation provides a clean and informative test of the specified configuration.
